title: A complex whose identity is homotopic to zero is exact
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $K_\bullet$ a chain complex of left $A$-modules indexed by $\mathbf N$ (differentials $d:K_{n+1}\to K_n$, $K_{-1}=0$). Suppose given $A$-linear maps $h_n:K_n\to K_{n+1}$ ($n\geq0$) with $d\circ h_n+h_{n-1}\circ d=\mathrm{id}_{K_n}$ for all $n\geq0$ (where $h_{-1}\circ d=0$ for $n=0$), i.e. a homotopy from $\mathrm{id}_{K_\bullet}$ to $0$. Then $K_\bullet$ is exact in every degree: $H_n(K_\bullet)=0$ for all $n\geq0$. (More generally, for any complex shape and any preadditive category with homology, a homotopy $\mathrm{id}\simeq0$ makes every homology object zero.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AT (lemma-homology-complex), last paragraph of the proof: exactness of the extended complex is deduced from the homotopy n_(s_0..s_p) -> n_(s,s_0..s_p); the general fact that a complex homotopic to zero (identity null-homotopic) has zero homology is the standard one used there
